A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 23-page versions of the same work, including Appendices A–D. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures and appendix table.

before.justification: V2 reports theoretical results, proofs and exact symbolic computations using Macaulay2 in Appendix D. These mathematical examples do not constitute experiments, simulations, user studies or data analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains the theoretical results and symbolic examples. Neither its main text nor its appendices report original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The polynomial MLP and CNN architectures, parametrizations, activation assumptions and mean-squared-error formulation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical datasets or tasks. The symbolic MLP and CNN examples in Appendix D retain the same coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated empirical baselines. The theoretical comparisons with other architectures and prior mathematical results are unchanged.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocol appears in either version. The theoretical regression setting and Appendix D architecture, activation and stride choices remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The nodal and cuspidal examples in Appendix A and symbolic network analyses in Appendix D are retained unchanged. No ablation or robustness study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty intervals, significance tests or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The stated findings and symbolic example results are unchanged, including rank 3 in equation (64), dimension 4 in equation (65), and the Appendix D.2 table. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: After equation (6), the proof of Theorem 4.2 changes λ from a real scalar to a polynomial and explicitly states that both f_W and λ remain unchanged when the selected weight row varies. This locally corrects the linear-independence argument; theorem statements and appendix proofs retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about identifiability, neuromanifold dimensions, subnetwork singularities and differing critical exposedness of MLPs and CNNs.

C2.justification: The sparsity-bias interpretation and limitations remain unchanged, including incomplete characterization of MLP singularities, unresolved critical-point types and proposed extensions beyond polynomial activations.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same model specifications and Macaulay2 computation descriptions. No implementation details or code/data access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged, preserving the positioning relative to neuroalgebraic geometry, implicit sparsity bias and singular learning theory.

P1.justification: V3 locally revises the proof paragraph, removes an extra period in Theorem 4.2, standardizes several 'equation' references and updates the arXiv stamp. Section organization and the broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3, their captions and placement, the appendix table and displayed equations are unchanged. The page layout is retained apart from incidental line wrapping following text edits.

improvement.justification: V3 repairs a local mathematical inaccuracy in Theorem 4.2's proof by identifying λ as a polynomial and explicitly preserving it under the weight-row variation. This makes the tangent-space dimension argument more accurate and clearer, while the theorem scope, conclusions and appendix evidence remain unchanged.
